regions.region: page 1 title, author block, abstract, and graphical abstract
regions.finding: Verified the true article title and aggregate current method. The graphical abstract repeats the generic 22-example/56–91% reaction class and is linked to one general-scheme record rather than treated as a single experiment.

Four separately drawn, explicitly cited prior-work reaction classes were classified as literature examples: Rh C–H allenylation, Rh/Ag hydroarylation, Pd/H+ allene formation, and Pd carbonylative acid/ester formation.
The generic current Rh carbonylation retains desired allenone as not observed and unexpected 2(3H)-furanones as the product class; individual Table 1/Scheme 2 runs are represented separately.
Two example bioactive compounds are contextual molecular examples, not reaction arrows or current-paper preparations; no experiment record was fabricated.

unresolved: Scheme 1 structures use generic R/Ar/DG labels and do not specify experiment-level quantities or yields.
The article advertises Supporting Information, but workspace SI association is unestablished and no SI facts were imported.

regions.region: page 2 upper Table 1 reaction header, entries 1–11, and footnote a
regions.finding: Eleven independent optimization runs were retained with shared 1a/2b/Rh loading/solvent volume/25 °C/CO balloon/12 h conditions, row catalyst and solvent, recovery of 1a, five product-specific NMR yields, and the dibromomethane measurement basis.
Narrative observations map to Table 1 rows and were not duplicated. Entry 4 is identified as optimal; entries 5/6 explicitly give zero furanone and 98%/87% recovery.

The text introduces the 22 Scheme 2 experiments shown on page 3. Two additional named heteroaryl-boronic-acid trials were retained separately as qualitative poor-yield/poor-selectivity records because numerical details are SI-only.

The catalytic cycle is classified as mechanism. A separately stated 13CO experiment is retained as a partial reported experiment with only the main-text interpretation; missing isotope details were not inferred from unavailable SI.

unresolved: The two heteroaryl trials lack numeric yields/selectivities and operational details in the main article.
The 13CO experiment lacks substrates, conditions, labeled positions, and quantitative incorporation in the supplied source.
Most scope workups, purifications, and isolated masses are not printed in the main article.

regions.region: page 3 Scheme 2 common reaction header and footnotes a/b
regions.finding: The shared 1.0 mmol alcohol/2.0 mmol boronic acid/5 mol% Rh(acac)(C2H4)2/5 mL THF/25 °C/CO-balloon conditions and crude-1H-NMR E/Z basis were applied to each displayed row. Footnote b explicitly overrides E-6ga to 10 mol% catalyst.

Twenty-two distinct substrate-scope experiments were retained with their displayed times, isolated yields, and E/Z ratios where printed. E-6ba and Z-6ba are two outcomes of one experiment, not duplicate reactions.

regions.region: page 3 ORTEP images for Z-6ba and E-6ga
regions.finding: CCDC 2324116 and 2324113 support the source stereochemical assignments for existing scope products. They are characterization, not preparations and not machine-structure verification.
The sentence completing the alternative G′ route belongs to the proposed Scheme 3 mechanism shown on page 4; no intermediate preparation or yield was created.

unresolved: No E/Z ratio is printed for 6na, 6ra, or 6sa.
Complex scope products remain label-based with null SMILES where stereochemical encoding was uncertain.
Main-text workups, purification details, and isolated masses are not available.

regions.finding: A–G/G′ form a proposed double-CO-insertion catalytic cycle. They were classified as mechanistic intermediates, not isolated experimental stages.

regions.region: page 4 Supporting Information and Accession Codes
regions.finding: The page states online SI availability and CCDC 2324113/2324116. Workspace SI association remains unestablished; CCDC data were linked only as characterization for E-6ga/Z-6ba and not treated as SI or new reactions.

Bibliography and contextual prior literature only; cited external papers were not expanded into current-paper experiments.
